advisory.finding: `PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE` is defined but never passed by any production caller. Only `DEFAULT` (claim gate, attest.py:764) and `DRIFT_REFRESH` (attest.py:178) are wired; the completion/close gate uses kind `completion-verifier`, whose branch in `compute_validity` never reads `profile`. `CLOSE` is dead in production and can only mislead a future maintainer into assuming a close-gate consumes it.

The mapping-shaped return and profile selection are already verified behaviorally in tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py (compute_validity returns {'valid':...,'health':...}); the AST checks add no behavioral regression coverage and break on a pure refactor.
advisory.finding: test_compute_validity_callers.py asserts on the AST/source structure of call sites of compute_validity across src/rebar (tuple-vs-name binding, subscript/.get consumption, a keyword literally named 'profile') rather than on any observable behavior — it is source-grepping the unit under test and a change-detector that breaks on behavior-preserving refactors (renaming the local result variable, extracting a consumer helper, passing profile positionally, or relocating a caller).
scenarios: A developer renames the `validity` local, extracts a helper that reads `validity['valid']`, or passes profile positionally — behavior identical, test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the AST-walk tests; rely on the behavioral tests that call compute_validity with each PlanValidityProfile and assert the returned {'valid','verdict','health'} mapping directly.
